notes: Third-party scanner run. DeepSec 2.3.10 is invoked unchanged through its own CLI: scan (regex matchers), process (Claude Agent SDK investigation), export (findings as JSON). No DeepSec code is modified and nothing is written to the installed workspace.

The adapter builds a private DeepSec workspace inside the run's raw output with one project, no plugins, and ai: {mode: local, provider: local}, so the run uses the operator's own CLI login and no API key is configured or recorded.
The DeepSec root is operator-specific. It is written with a leading ~ so it expands to the operator's home rather than pinning one machine; point it at your own workspace.

Cost bound: limit 6 with batch_size 3 and concurrency 1 means at most two agent batches per input, six files each run, three inputs. Haiku is the deliberate choice because this is a pipeline exercise, not a model comparison, so the cheapest capable route is the right one. Raise limit only for a run whose purpose needs it, and expect cost to rise with it roughly linearly.

Because limit 6 leaves most of each repository scanned but never investigated, every invocation of this run is recorded as partial with error code scope_incomplete and bundles_resolved false. That is correct and expected: no model opened those files, so silence about them is not a negative result and the run must not earn quiet credit for them. Raise limit to cover a whole input if a run needs a complete observation of it.
Cost and token numbers in the result are DeepSec's own per-file shares of each batch, summed back into batch totals. They are CLI-reported estimates, never a bill.
max_turns 60 is well below DeepSec's default of 150 and bounds a batch that goes in circles; a batch that hits it is recorded as a batch that reached no verdict, not as a clean scan.
Content-mode traces stay local; they contain the source that was sent to the model, and the imported Claude Code transcripts contain the tool results the agent read.

Tool calls, context selection and per-turn model events come only from the Claude Code transcripts the agent sessions leave under ~/.claude/projects. A run whose transcripts have been cleaned up records those categories as unavailable, which is not evidence that no tool ran. docs/DEEPSEC.md carries the full capture matrix.
